dependencies.name: Vertex AI implicit context caching

existing.currentVersion: implicitly on; not measured (cachedContentTokenCount not read)

findings: VERIFIED (Gemini API caching doc, updated 2026-09-02): implicit caching is enabled by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer. Minimum input token count is 4,096 for Gemini 3.5/3.6/3.7/3.8 Flash and 3.1 Pro, and 2,048 for 2.5 Flash/Pro. Guidance: 'put large and common contents at the beginning of your prompt'. A request hits the cache when it shares a common prefix with a recent request.

VERIFIED (Vertex overview, via search snippet of the official page): implicit caching is on for all Google Cloud projects and gives a 90% discount on cached tokens versus standard input tokens. Hits are more likely when requests with the same prefix arrive close together. The Gemini 3 minimum is 4,096 tokens.
VERIFIED (docs): the hit size is reported as usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount.

Prefix must be at the start: VERIFIED in substance. Caching matches a common prefix, so any byte that varies before the static block breaks the hit for everything after it. This confirms the brief's finding that 'Required envelope kind' and 'Writable step IDs' (GatewayPayloadSerializer.java:22-28) sit between the output contract and the syntax reference and cap any hit at the 2.4 KB contract.

Does systemInstruction count as prefix: INFERRED yes, MEDIUM confidence. Evidence: python-genai issue #1880 (Vertex, gemini-2.5-flash) reports that identical system instructions reliably cache on the second call. It also reports erratic hit rates (~42%) when system prompts share a ~10K-token prefix but differ in suffix. Google docs do not state the serialization order explicitly.

Reliability caveats (VERIFIED as reported bugs, not as Vertex behavior): python-genai #2064 (Gemini API, gemini-3-flash-preview) reports a 'dead zone' where cachedContentTokenCount drops to 0 for prompts of ~9K-17K tokens despite a byte-identical prefix, with ~2K-token cache granularity below ~8K. Implicit hits are best-effort and cannot be relied on for a numeric target.

Size check, INFERRED: output-contract.md is 2,436 B and syntax-reference.md is 6,766 B (VERIFIED), 9,202 B together, which is roughly 2,300-2,700 tokens at 3.4-4 chars/token (not tokenized). The static prefix alone is BELOW the 4,096-token minimum. A hit therefore needs the whole request to be at least 4,096 tokens, and even then only the static ~2.5K tokens are shared across different tests. Only same-test repair attempts and repeated compiles share more (the fenced source).

Additional prefix-instability risk, INFERRED from VERIFIED code: providerSchema() (GenAiLlmGatewayClient.java:326-374) embeds the per-request writable step IDs and kind in responseJsonSchema. It is built with Map.of, whose iteration order is randomized per JVM (JDK ImmutableCollections SALT), so the schema's JSON key order can differ between replicas and restarts. Whether Vertex places the response schema inside the cacheable prefix is UNKNOWN. If it does, both effects defeat caching. Fix cheaply with deterministic (sorted/LinkedHashMap) schema construction.

Expected value, INFERRED: with FR-11 applied, a hit saves about 90% of ~2.5K input tokens per call. That is small next to output plus thinking tokens for a multi-step FULL compile. The main efficiency levers are (1) INCREMENTAL output scaling with suffix length (NFR-1), (2) thinking level, and (3) deduplicating global context (FR-12). Caching is a secondary, best-effort gain and should be measured, not promised.

alternatives: Explicit cachedContent (see next entry; not recommended)
conflicts: Behind R2D2, whether the proxy preserves the billing and caching path and returns cachedContentTokenCount is UNKNOWN (SPK-01).

dependencies.name: Vertex AI explicit context caching (cachedContent)
findings: VERIFIED (SDK jar): GenerateContentConfig.cachedContent(String) and CreateCachedContentConfig exist in 1.71.0.

VERIFIED (docs table): the same per-model minimum applies, 4,096 tokens for Gemini 3.x. The ~2.5K-token static prefix (INFERRED size) is too small to be an explicit cache unless padded. Padding defeats the purpose.

VERIFIED (reported API error text in search results): 'CachedContent cannot be used with GenerateContent request setting system_instruction, tools or tool_config'. The system instruction has to live inside the cache, which couples the cache resource to the prompt pin.
VERIFIED (third-party article, MEDIUM credibility): explicit caches carry TTL-based storage charges per token-hour and must be created, refreshed and deleted as a regional resource.

INFERRED: operational cost (create/TTL/refresh per model, region and prompt pin; storage billing; an extra endpoint through R2D2 that may not be allowlisted) outweighs the gain for a sub-minimum prefix. Implicit caching already gives the same 90% discount on hits.

alternatives: Implicit caching with a byte-stable leading prefix (FR-11)

collisions.title: Planner change detection ignores 10.35 context and 10.44 reference policy
collisions.detail: CompilationPlanner.Step is (UUID id, String text), and the changed-prefix scan uses Step.equals (CompilationPlanner.java:17, 81-84). A change that is only in a step's context entries (VariableReference / SecretReference / ContextualDefault) or in globalContext leaves text equal. The planner would then call the step unchanged and could select REUSE (UNCHANGED_SOURCE) or lock a step whose meaning changed. This matters directly for the user's scenario ('step 2 uses a different username variable') when the variable is bound via step context rather than a <var> token in the text. Required: per-step equality over text + step context + that step's reference_policy entry (StepReferencePolicyDeriver output). Any globalContext change or change to globally allowed defaults selects FULL (a structural, non-English signal).

Q1_genai_vertex.summary: The SDK supports systemInstruction, thinkingConfig (thinkingLevel/thinkingBudget) and both usage fields (VERIFIED in the jar). For gemini-3.8-flash: default thinking MEDIUM; LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH allowed; MINIMAL errors; never send budget and level together (VERIFIED, Gemini API docs). Implicit caching is on by default at a 90% discount, with a 4,096-token minimum for Gemini 3.x (VERIFIED). The prefix must lead the request. systemInstruction is INFERRED to be part of the cacheable prefix. Explicit cachedContent is NOT worth it: the ~9.2 KB static prefix is ~2.3-2.7K tokens, below the 4,096 minimum, it is exclusive with request systemInstruction, and it adds storage/TTL operations.

Exact token count of the static prefix (not tokenized; use countTokens in SPK-01)

Q2_prompt_design_prior_code.summary: No study was found that directly measures 'prior code for the writable step as a diff anchor' in NL-to-code regeneration. The available evidence is indirect: (a) instructional code-editing benchmarks (CanItEdit, arXiv 2312.12450) show models can edit provided code well when the instruction states the change, which supports the anchor; (b) anchoring-bias studies on LLMs (arXiv 2412.06593) find that initial and authoritative-looking information disproportionately sways outputs, and a 2026 code-review study (arXiv 2603.18740) found explicit debiasing instructions recover most of the loss; (c) Olausson et al. (ICLR 2024, arXiv 2306.09896) find repair gains are modest and bottlenecked by feedback quality, which supports giving the rejected proposal plus precise diagnostics on repair (FR-10) rather than blind retries.
Q2_prompt_design_prior_code.recommendation: INFERRED design. (1) Locked prefix: always send English + baseline code, marked READ-ONLY / 'already executed, page state after these steps'. This is low bias risk and needed for selector/state continuity (decisions OQ-2 item 3). (2) Writable steps whose text is unchanged (for example step 3 in the user's example): send prior code as a 'last known good for this exact text' anchor. That is lower risk because the intent is unchanged. (3) The edited step(s): send English only by default, or prior code labeled 'SUPERSEDED — written for different text: <old text>'. The 10.26 harness should compare arm A (no anchor) vs arm B (labeled anchor) on the edited step, with a planted-mutation metric that counts stale-identifier carry-over (for example the old variable name surviving). Keep whichever wins, and pin the choice in PROMPT_VERSION.

Q3_restore_sizing.summary: About 900 lines of main code (Controller 67 + Service 455 + DTOs 111 + a new compileVersioned-equivalent of ~80 lines, plus a merged attempt loop of ~250 lines) and ~730 lines of tests (3 archived test files) must be re-ported, not cherry-picked. Planner/assembler/capture store/budget and the FE v2 UI are already on the branch unchanged. Collisions COL-1..COL-5 are data-model and migration issues that the archive never faced because it predates V21-V24. They, not the REST layer, are the critical path.

precedent: C0 already names GLOBAL_OR_FORWARD_SCOPE as a FULL reason and says 'A model/heuristic may flag uncertainty but cannot establish trust or enlarge its own write set' (studio-inference-contract-v1.md:22, 51). A detector that only escalates to FULL is C0-conformant. The default forward trust (OQ-2 item 1) is the part that needs the C0 amendment signed by Aria (CON-2).

Lexicon and NL-pattern detection of cross-references is established in requirements and legal engineering: Adedjouma, Sabetzadeh, Briand RE'14 and Sannier et al., Requirements Engineering 2017 (detection and resolution of legal cross-references with NL patterns).

Lexicon detection of universal quantifiers ('all', 'every', 'always') is a known 'requirements smell': Femmer et al., JSS 2017. Reported average precision 59% at recall 82%, with high variation. Expect a similar FP-heavy, FN-nonzero profile.

minimalLexicon.scope: Apply only to the text of changed steps (after Unicode NFKC + lowercase). A hit escalates to FULL with reason GLOBAL_OR_FORWARD_SCOPE (logged as ESCALATED_FULL, with the matched rule id, never the text).

rules.note: 'step 1', 'step #2'. Backward only if the number is below the step's own index. Otherwise it is forward, which is fine because the suffix is regenerated anyway.

deliberatelyExcluded: 'again' (for example 'log in again' is a normal forward step, very high FP)
bare 'above' / 'below' (spatial locators: 'the button above the table')
'go back' alone (navigation intent is expressed via page.goto; excluding it avoids FP)

risks.falsePositives: Moderate. Numbered references to later steps and quantifiers over UI elements that happen to match noun lists. Cost: an unnecessary FULL, which is visible and correct but slower. Mitigate by requiring the step noun/number relation and by logging rule ids to tune from telemetry.
risks.falseNegatives: Unavoidable. Paraphrase ('use the account from the login'), implicit semantic backward dependency (step 2 now needs a different start URL that step 1 sets), and non-English text. The nets are the model PREFIX_IMPACT outcome, the whole-artifact validator, FULL_REBUILD_REQUIRED on reused-code failure, and always-FULL execution from step 1 (CON-1). A runtime failure caused by an FN shows up as a red run, and 'Rebuild all steps' is the recovery. The spec should state this residual risk explicitly (NFR-6).
risks.evaluation: Build a labeled edit corpus in the 10.26 harness (for example 50 edits, including planted backward dependencies). Report detector precision/recall and PREFIX_IMPACT agreement. Treat numbers as proposed targets pending Pax/Aria (CON-10).
